newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Pangang Steel 1996 profit soars.
newsitem.headline: China's Pangang Steel 1996 profit soars.

text.p: China's Pangang Group Steel Plate Co said on Thursday its 1996 net profit rose sharply to 90.16 million yuan ($10.86 million) from 31.35 million yuan in 1995 on cuts in production and marketing costs.
In 1996, the company's turnover was 1.81 billion yuan, up 49.33 percent from 1.21 billion yuan in 1995, the company's annual report published in Wednesday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
The company planned to issue a cash dividend of 0.19 yuan per share based on its 1996 profits, which would be tabled at a forthcoming annual general meeting of shareholders, it said.

Pangang, which makes steel plates for China's automobile, railway and ship building industries, said earnings were capped by lower sale prices, but were helped by success in reducing production and marketing costs. It did not elaborate.

Pangang, headquartered in Panzhihua city in southwestern Sichuan province, said its accounts receivable hit 510.22 million yuan at the end of 1996, up from 452.65 million yuan at the beginning of last year.

Analysts said Pangang, like other big state-run firms in China, is plagued by triangular debt -- difficulty in getting payment for delivered goods that curtails cash flow -- which could lead to a shortage of working capital.
Pangang listed 62 million A shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in November 1996. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
